item.title: Earth's Increasing Mass: Re: Earth's Increasing Mass
item.content:encoded:
The increase is so small that it'll likely take millions of years (at least) to be noticeable. The scale between something like us and the Earth is equivalent to a molecule compared to a human. You'd need a lot of mass to noticeably impact the Earth, just as you'll need a lot of molecules to noticably impact the weight of a human.

What's that? How many molecules do you need to add to a person to make a noticeable impact on their weight? Glad you asked! Lots! As in, we need to use scientific notation to accurately depict the amount. An example: 1 mol of water is 6.02214076x1023 individual water molecules. Now, 1 mol of water weighs about 18 grams (18.015 grams to be exact) For comparison, 1 kilogram is 100 grams, and 1 ounce is about 28 grams. One mol of water weighs a little over half an ounce.

Similarily, we'll need mols of grams (not an appropriate use of the mol, but good enough for our purposes) to noticeably impact the Earth's mass.

So yeah, the stuff added by the SCPs you named are basically drops in the bucket compared to Earth's overall mass.

item.title: Earth's Increasing Mass: Earth's Increasing Mass
item.content:encoded: I am wondering if the Foundation has any plan for dealing with all the excess mass that results from these SCPs. They've found short-term ways to keep the Keter cakes from overrunning the planet, but the mass of the consumed cakes is still conserved by D-class digestion. The same goes for 646's terminated offspring and 1680's clones of Tyler Buchanan used as D-class. The mass of the SCP-verse's planet Earth is gradually increasing and, without some way to destroy all that mass or send it somewhere else, will continue to do so. Are there other anomalies that are constantly destroying mass and therefore balancing this somewhat? Or is the increase so small that it simply won't matter against the mass of the entire planet?

item.title: Inter-Site Rivalries: Re: Inter-Site Rivalries
item.content:encoded:
Some entries mention sites/ departments that stereotypical "Do nothing all day". Because they contain/ research really obscure/ rare kinds of anomalous phenomena.

The most common example is the Antimemetics Divison, who get accused of doing nothing all day because nobody actually remembers what they did all day. But the Essophysics Division (And by extension Site-76), Legal Division, and a handful of others are all stereotyped in various articles.

item.title: A question about the Anomalous Intelligence Community: Re: A question about the Anomalous Intelligence Community
item.content:encoded:
I remember in the U.I.U introductory tale there is a mention of "Suits" who are individuals (Presumably also controlled by the pentagon) whom deal with anomalous phenomena. But I don't know of any other tales they appear in.

One thing to remember is that most of the U.S.A's soldiers, agents, and so on that are versed in anomalous phenomena probably work on behalf of the G.O.C and not the U.S government. The U.I.U is just a group of lackies, probation agents, and loose cannons in the F.B.I who are put into what everyone else thinks is a joke unit.

Most of the reason the U.I.U even exists still is that they mostly operate within their own borders. If the U.S had an anomalous division that investigated foreign affairs they would very quickly discover just how outgunned, out-manned, and out-planned they really are.

item.title: A question about the Anomalous Intelligence Community: A question about the Anomalous Intelligence Community
item.content:encoded:
Not in the sense of groups like the GOC, Foundation and so on and so forth where the Unusual Incidents Unit calling them their 'rivals' would be paying themselves a pretty generous compliment, but instead I mean… well, doing a dive into the UIU hub it occurred to me that the FBI is largely limited in scope to inside of the United States.

Which is all well and good… but, the United States has interests outside of its own borders.

The CIA, conversely, operates mostly abroad as a covert agency.

So, my question is: Does the CIA have its own equivalent to the UIU, or would they borrow a 'specialist' from them in the event they have to deal with something anomalous? Or do they simply hand it off to the Foundation, or the GOC or someone similar?

Has this been addressed in a tale or on one of the hubs?
